subject: Intermittent control-plane connection flaps — update and next steps
messages:
From: Thomas Miller <tmiller@blueoakhealth.com>

Cc: platform@blueoakhealth.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: API failures this morning — intermittent control-plane disconnects

Hi Priya,

We started seeing intermittent failures against our private deployment this morning between ~08:45–09:05 PDT. Client services report 502/connection reset errors when calling the Redwood API; downstream workers that depend on agent heartbeats restarted themselves several times. I attached a short diagnostics log (connection-diagnostics-06014.log) — you'll see repeated TLS handshake failures and abrupt TCP resets.

Impact: several queued jobs failed and were retried, resulting in a processing backlog for yesterday's batch. We have temporarily scaled workers down to reduce thrash but would like your team's help identifying whether this is a control-plane issue on your side or a config/agent regression on ours.

Can someone from infra or account ops confirm? This is affecting one production service but not all traffic; we can share more logs if helpful.

Thanks,
Thomas Miller
Director, Platform Engineering
BlueOak Health

Attachments: connection-diagnostics-06014.log (text/plain, 42KB)

Subject: RE: API failures this morning — intermittent control-plane disconnects

Thanks Priya — I've pulled the attached log and correlated it against our control-plane telemetry. Quick findings:

1) We saw a short spike in control-plane CPU and accept queue depth at 08:50 PDT for the BlueOak cluster only.
2) A recent Helm chart update (v2.18.3 -> v2.19.0) pushed a change to our agent-side keepalive/livenessProbe timing on 2027-06-13 22:12 UTC. That change reduced aggressive keepalive frequency but inadvertently widened the window before reconnect backoff, which in the presence of a transient network jitter produced a connection storm as many agents retried simultaneously.
3) The combination of the accept queue spike and a bug in our TLS rehandshake path then caused abrupt resets instead of graceful reconnects for a subset of connections; that matches the TCP reset pattern in your log.

Mitigation applied (11:30 PDT):
- Rolled back the agent liveness change for BlueOak's control plane and restored prior backoff parameters.
- Increased the accept queue size temporarily and enabled an emergency rate limit for incoming agent reconnections for the affected control-plane nodes.

Status now: we've observed a drop in connection resets and no new job restarts in the last 25 minutes. We're running a 2-hour watch window and will keep you posted.

Next steps:
- We'll prepare a short runbook with recommended temporary tunings you can apply if you run into restarts while we finalize the fix. (Attaching runbook now.)
- Postmortem planned; target delivery with RCA and remediation plan by Wed 16 Jun EOD.

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Update: intermittent connection resets — action taken and next steps

Hi Thomas — quick update and apologies for the disruption.

What we found (short): a recent agent liveness/backoff change combined with transient network jitter created a rapid reconnect pattern that briefly overwhelmed a subset of control-plane nodes, producing the abrupt TLS/TCP resets you saw.

What we did:
- Rolled back the liveness/backoff changes for your VPC cluster and applied a temporary rate limit on reconnections.
- Pushed a configuration tweak to increase the accept queue and enable a more conservative rehandshake path while we build a permanent fix.
- Placed the cluster on a 2-hour elevated watch and collected additional diagnostics (attached).

Impact and ETA: we've seen no new job restarts since ~11:20 PDT. We expect stabilization across the cluster; engineering will deliver a controlled patch to prevent recurrence and we'll share the postmortem by EOD Wed 16 Jun.

Ask of you: please hold off on agent upgrades or key rotations in the BlueOak environment until we confirm the permanent fix. If you prefer, we can coordinate a maintenance window and apply the patch for you.

Separately, I know this caused processing delays — if you'd like, I can escalate for a formal SLA credit review and coordinate with billing.

Again, sorry for the disruption. Will follow up with the full RCA.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
